record.paper_title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
record.context_brief: embedded cmc surfaces with circular boundary
record.original_question: Let Σ be a compact embedded surface in ℝ³ with constant mean curvature and boundary equal to a round circle. Must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by that circle or one of the spherical caps bounded by that circle?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. Is a compact embedded cmc surface of ℝ³ spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a round circle, and let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact, connected, embedded smooth surface with constant mean curvature whose boundary $\partial \Sigma$ equals $C$. Must $\Sigma$ be either the flat planar disk bounded by $C$ or one of the two spherical caps bounded by $C$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely cited as open. While many partial results exist (e.g., uniqueness under stability for disk-type surfaces by Alías–López–Palmer, and uniqueness under local convexity or symmetry assumptions), the general question of whether a compact embedded CMC surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ spanning a circle must be a planar disk or spherical cap remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space (Lopez survey)
status_evidence.snippet: It is still unknown whether the spherical caps are the only examples of compact embedded surfaces with nonzero constant mean curvature bounded by a circle.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem for compact embedded CMC surfaces with circular boundary remains open.

status_evidence.title: An extension of Liebmann's Theorem to hypersurfaces with boundary
status_evidence.snippet: It is an open question whether a compact embedded hypersurface with CMC and spherical boundary is necessarily a hyperplanar ball or a spherical cap, even in the simplest case of a CMC surface in R^3 bounded by a circle.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly stated as open in recent literature.
